objects.name: Exmatter
objects.description: A custom exfiltration tool used by ransomware operators to steal user files, databases, and compressed files. It uploads data to a preconfigured server via SFTP.  It also has anti-forensic capabilities and can use a WebDav client as a secondary exfiltration method.

objects.name: Ryuk Infostealer
objects.description: An exfiltration tool capable of programmatic identification and automatic exfiltration of data.

objects.name: StealBit
objects.description: An exfiltration tool capable of programmatic identification and automatic exfiltration of data, associated with the LockBit 2.0 operator.

objects.name: Conti Ransomware
objects.description: A ransomware group that a newer variant of Exmatter was observed being used with for exfiltration.

objects.name: Exmatter
objects.description: Custom exfiltration tool that iterates through folders, prioritizes recently modified files, and excludes directories within 'C:\ProgramData\'. It uses SFTP to exfiltrate data, with options for WebDav failover and a SOCKS5 proxy.

objects.name: PowerShell
objects.description: Used by Exmatter to overwrite the file and delete itself after exfiltration, employing anti-forensic techniques.

objects.name: ADFind
objects.description: Tool used for network and Active Directory administration that can be abused for reconnaissance.

objects.name: Advanced IP Scanner
objects.description: Tool used for network scanning that can be abused for reconnaissance.

objects.name: Windows Sysinternals suite
objects.description: Legitimately signed binaries that can be used for malicious activities like credential dumping (Procdump) and malware/ransomware deployment (PsExec).

objects.name: Themida
objects.description: Anti-reverse engineering software protection utility used to protect the Exmatter executable.

objects.name: Kroll's Threat Intelligence team reports more than 200 ransomware threat actor groups
objects.description: Kroll's Threat Intelligence team tracks more than 200 ransomware threat actor groups based on over 3,200 incident response engagements in 2021.

objects.name: BlackMatter
objects.description: Originally associated with the BlackMatter Ransomware-as-a-Service (RaaS) operation, but variants are now used by other RaaS groups.

objects.name: Targeting specific file extensions (web/application source code, Remote Desktop shortcuts, CAD/GIS files)
Use of legitimate tools for reconnaissance
